title: Getting started with a5R
text: Map longitude/latitude coordinate cell given resolution (0–30). Higher resolutions produce smaller cells. Convert back cell centre point:
code: cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10) cell #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 6344be8000000000 a5_cell_to_lonlat(cell) #> <wk_xy[1] with CRS=OGC:CRS84> #> [1] (-3.183746 55.9806)

title: Getting started with a5R
text: Get boundary polygon one cells:  Boundaries returned wk_wkb vectors default (set format = "wkt" WKT). integrate directly sf, terra, spatial tooling via wk package.

title: Getting started with a5R
text: A5 hierarchical grid: every cell parent coarser resolution 4 children next finer resolution. can visualise relationship - parent (dark outline) contains cell (blue fill), turn contains 4 children (orange):  Cell area decreases geometrically — level roughly 4x smaller:
code: parent <- a5_cell_to_parent(cell) parent #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 6344be0000000000  children <- a5_cell_to_children(cell) children #> <a5_cell[4]> #> [1] 6344be2000000000 6344be6000000000 6344bea000000000 6344bee000000000 plot(NULL, xlim = c(-3.23, -3),  ylim = c(55.98, 55.99),                       xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1        ) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(a5_cell_to_children(cell)),      col = "#ad6e2020", border = "#ad6e20", add = TRUE) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(cell), col = "#206ead40", border = "#206ead",      lwd = 2, add = TRUE) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(parent), border = "#333333", lwd = 2, add = TRUE) a5_cell_area(0:5) #> Units: [m^2] #> [1] 4.250547e+13 8.501094e+12 2.125273e+12 5.313184e+11 1.328296e+11 #> [6] 3.320740e+10

title: Getting started with a5R
text: complete set siblings present, a5_compact() merges back shared parent. inverse a5_cell_to_children() useful reducing size large cell sets without losing coverage. Many a5R functions return compacted output automatically. example, a5_grid_disk() a5_spherical_cap() compact results — use a5_uncompact() need uniform-resolution grid (see Traversal ).
code: children #> <a5_cell[4]> #> [1] 6344be2000000000 6344be6000000000 6344bea000000000 6344bee000000000 a5_compact(children) #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 6344be8000000000  # round-trips back to the original a5_uncompact(a5_compact(children), resolution = 11) #> <a5_cell[4]> #> [1] 6344be2000000000 6344be6000000000 6344bea000000000 6344bee000000000

title: Getting started with a5R
text: Find neighbouring cells hop count a5_grid_disk(), great-circle distance a5_spherical_cap():   functions return compacted cell vector — sibling groups merged coarser parent cells save space. recover uniform grid original resolution, pass result a5_uncompact():
code: disk <- a5_grid_disk(cell, k = 10) cap <- a5_spherical_cap(cell, radius = 50000)  plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(cap), col = "#6ead2020", border = "#6ead20", asp = 1) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(disk), col = "#206ead20", border = "#206ead", asp = 1) disk_grid <- a5_uncompact(disk, resolution = a5_get_resolution(cell))  plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(disk_grid), col = "#206ead20", border = "#206ead", asp = 1)

title: Getting started with a5R
text: a5_grid() convenience function provided a5R (part underlying a5 Rust crate) returns cells target resolution covering given area — handy binning, zonal statistics, spatial analysis workflows common R. Pass bounding box numeric vector:  geometry wk can handle works — polygons, sf objects, even a5_cell vectors:
code: cells <- a5_grid(c(-3.3, 55.9, -3.1, 56.0), resolution = 12) length(cells) #> [1] 90  plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells), col = "#206ead20", border = "#206ead", asp = 1) library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE demo(nc, ask = FALSE, echo = FALSE) nca5 <- a5_grid(nc, resolution = 9) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(nca5), col = "#6d20ad20", border = "#6d20adff", asp = 1)

title: Multi-threading
text: can also set threads package load time via R option environment variable - useful scripts batch jobs: a5_set_threads() invisibly returns previous value, making temporary changes easy:
code: # Check the current setting (default: 1) a5_get_threads() #> [1] 1  # Use 4 threads a5_set_threads(4) a5_get_threads() #> [1] 4 # In .Rprofile or at the top of a script options(a5R.threads = 4)  # Or as an environment variable # Sys.setenv(A5R_NUM_THREADS = 4) old <- a5_set_threads(4) # ... parallel work ... a5_set_threads(old)

title: Multi-threading
text: Threading applies vectorised functions process element independently: Scalar bulk operations (a5_cell_to_children(), a5_compact(), a5_cell_area(), etc.) unaffected — already fast delegate algorithms don’t parallelise element-wise.

title: Multi-threading
text: Threading small fixed overhead (thread synchronisation, memory allocation intermediate results). small vectors can outweigh benefit. rule thumb: < 1,000 elements: stick 1 thread 1,000–10,000: 2-4 threads helps heavy ops (boundary, indexing) > 10,000: use many threads cores ’s quick comparison 100k cells: Note user time increases (total CPU work across threads) elapsed (wall-clock) time decreases — ’s parallelism work.
code: cells <- a5_grid(c(-10, 50, 10, 60), resolution = 12) length(cells) #> [1] 704259  a5_set_threads(1) system.time(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells, format = "wkt")) #>   user  system elapsed #>  3.124   0.000   3.122   a5_set_threads(8) system.time(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells, format = "wkt")) #>   user  system elapsed #> 6.195   1.289   1.667

title: Multi-threading
text: a5R uses dedicated rayon thread pool, separate R’s parallelism. safe use alongside future, mirai, etc. think carefully nested parallelism can, overloaded, degrade performance. thread pool rebuilt time call a5_set_threads(), changing count mid-session fine (cheap) free - ideally, just start workflow rather toggling per-call.

title: Traversal and distance
text: Pick origin cell use a5_spherical_cap() grab every cell whose centre falls within given great-circle radius. result compacted, pass a5_uncompact() uniform-resolution grid. a5_grid_disk() selects cells hop count rather metric distance. vertex = FALSE (default) edge-sharing neighbours traversed (4-connected), producing diamond shape. Setting vertex = TRUE includes corner-sharing neighbours (8-connected), giving squarer footprint.
code: origin <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(35, 55, resolution = 14)  disk <- a5_grid_disk(origin, k = 20, vertex = FALSE) disk_vertex <- a5_grid_disk(origin, k = 20, vertex = TRUE) cap_compact <- a5_spherical_cap(origin, radius = 5000) cap <- a5_uncompact(cap_compact, resolution = 14)

title: Traversal and distance
text: Compute distance origin every cell cap (disk) visualise colour gradient.  Distance radiates smoothly centre — cells near origin dark, cells rim bright. origin cell shown white border reference.
code: dcap <- a5_cell_distance(origin, cap, units = "km") dcap_compact <- a5_cell_distance(origin, cap_compact, units = "km") ddisk <- a5_cell_distance(origin, disk, units = "km") ddisk_vertex <- a5_cell_distance(origin, disk_vertex, units = "km")  pal <- hcl.colors(256, "Inferno")  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1)) for (info in list(   list(s = disk, d = ddisk, lab = "Grid disk (edges)"),   list(s = disk_vertex, d = ddisk_vertex, lab = "Grid disk (vertices)"),   list(s = cap_compact, d = dcap_compact, lab = "Spherical cap (compact)"),   list(s = cap, d = dcap, lab = "Spherical cap") )) {   brk <- seq(0, max(as.numeric(info$d)), length.out = 257)   cols <- pal[findInterval(as.numeric(info$d), brk, all.inside = TRUE)]    plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(info$s), col = cols, border = NA, asp = 1,        main = info$lab)   plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(origin), border = "#ffffffff", add = TRUE) }

title: Traversal and distance
text: a5R supports three distance methods: haversine (great-circle), geodesic (WGS84 ellipsoid via Karney 2013), rhumb (loxodrome / constant-bearing). short distances nearly identical; differences grow distance.  difference near zero centre grows ~1675 m rim (~500 km away).
code: wide_origin <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(35, 55, resolution = 8) wide_cap <- a5_uncompact(   a5_spherical_cap(wide_origin, radius = 500000),   resolution = 8 )  hav <- a5_cell_distance(wide_origin, wide_cap, units = "m", method = "haversine") geo <- a5_cell_distance(wide_origin, wide_cap, units = "m", method = "geodesic")  diff_m <- as.numeric(geo - hav) brk <- seq(min(diff_m), max(diff_m), length.out = 257) cols <- pal[findInterval(diff_m, brk, all.inside = TRUE)]  layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1), widths = c(4, 1)) par(mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1)) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(wide_cap), col = cols, border = NA, asp = 1,      main = "Geodesic \u2212 Haversine (m)")  par(mar = c(9, 0, 9, 9)) image(1, seq(min(diff_m), max(diff_m), length.out = 256),       t(seq_along(pal)), col = pal, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") axis(4, las = 1)

title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: a5R provides R bindings A5 pentagonal geospatial index, powered a5 Rust crate via extendr. A5 partitions Earth’s surface pentagonal cells across 31 resolution levels. Cells equal-area, encoded 64-bit integers, achieve millimetre-level precision finest resolution.

title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: need working Rust toolchain (cargo rustc).

title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: See vignette("a5R") full walkthrough indexing, boundaries, hierarchy, traversal, grid generation.
code: library(a5R)  # Index a point to a cell cell <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10) cell #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 6344be8000000000  # Get the boundary polygon a5_cell_to_boundary(cell) #> <wk_wkb[1] with CRS=OGC:CRS84> #> [1] <POLYGON ((-3.175718 55.93546, -3.145905 55.97569, -3.151641 56.01921, -3.219413 56.00818, -3.226037 55.96443, -3.175718 55.93546...>  # Navigate the hierarchy a5_cell_to_parent(cell) #> <a5_cell[1]> #> [1] 6344be0000000000 a5_cell_to_children(cell) #> <a5_cell[4]> #> [1] 6344be2000000000 6344be6000000000 6344bea000000000 6344bee000000000 # Create a collection of cells whose centres fall within a great-circle distance of 100km from the origin cell cells <- a5_spherical_cap(cell, radius = 100000) |>    a5_uncompact(resolution = 10) plot(a5_cell_to_boundary(cells), col = "#206ead20", border = "#206ead", asp = 1)

title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: Vectorised Rust core — operations implemented Rust called R via extendr. Benchmarks confirm identical results Python, JavaScript, DuckDB A5 implementations. vctrs + wk integration — cell indices use a5_cell type tibble support; geometries return wk_wkb/wk_wkt vectors compatible sf terra. Grid generation — a5_grid() fills bounding box geometry cells target resolution using hierarchical flood-fill. Traversal — a5_grid_disk() a5_spherical_cap() select neighbours hop count great-circle distance. Multi-threading — opt-parallel processing via rayon vectorised operations. See vignette("multithreading").

title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: A5 created Felix Palmer. package thin R wrapper around work exist without . Query-farm team maintain DuckDB A5 extension, wraps Rust crate provided valuable reference project.

title: Generate a grid of A5 cells covering an area — a5_grid
text: Grid generation runs entirely Rust via hierarchical flood-fill bounding-box pruning. non-bbox geometry inputs, exact intersection filter removes cells fall outside target shape. cell count limit imposed — high resolutions large areas can consume significant memory. Input geometries must use WGS 84 coordinates; projected geometries reprojected produce incorrect results. Multiple geometries collected GEOMETRYCOLLECTION automatically. Antimeridian-crossing bounding boxes supported: xmin > xmax (e.g. c(170, -50, -170, -30)), bbox split antimeridian. Limitation: spatial filtering uses planar geometry lon/lat coordinates, can produce incomplete results close poles (~88° latitude) antimeridian. Use larger target geometry ensure complete coverage areas.
